title: Amphibious Aircraft Ontology — constraint file
description: A constraint file is a list of entries. Representation-neutral by design: this projects into OWL/RDF, SysML, or code. This schema is normative and is enforced in CI; schema/README.md is the prose companion, not the source of truth.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. cfr-25.527-a1. Must be unique across the whole corpus, not just within a file. Never reuse or repurpose an id: downstream consumers pin them.

kind.description: `table` covers requirements the CFR publishes as a lookup rather than an expression — § 25.807's exit dimensions and seats-per-exit-pair, for instance. It was invented downstream in flightforge's vendored copies before this schema existed, and is adopted here rather than rewritten, because a table really is what the regulation contains.

breakpoints.description: For piecewise-linear graph-valued terms: the labelled breakpoints the figure prints, recorded separately from the interpolating expression so the two can be cross-checked.

station.description: Prose label as printed on the figure.

body.description: Which body the station lies on. The forebody/afterbody split is what carries the discontinuity at the main step, which a single normalised axis cannot represent.

t.description: Normalised position within that body: 0 at its forward end, 1 at its aft end. Supplying body and t is what makes the figure machine-usable rather than prose; tools/run_tests.py interpolates on them.

statement.description: The constraint in prose. Required for assertion and qualitative entries — an entry whose substance lives only in verification.notes is not encoded, it is annotated.

id.description: An interpretation must be visibly one at the point of use. Downstream code that filters on id prefix must not have to open the file to find out.

authority.description: "14 CFR" | "CS-25" | "ANC-3" | "none" for an interpretation with no regulatory basis.

url.description: Canonical primary-source URL. Empty string only when authority is "none".

status.description: verified — matches primary regulatory text exactly. partial — text verified, but depends on a source not yet read. unverified — from a secondary source. interpretation — an engineering reading NOT stated in the regulation.

checked_against.description: What was actually read. "the regulation" is not an answer; name the endpoint, the issue date, or the image id.

sign_convention.description: Present only where the regulation's plain wording and its engineering reading differ in sign or in magnitude-vs-signed form. Stating it is mandatory there: an operator that silently contradicts the quoted text is the failure mode this corpus exists to prevent.

expression.description: Plain-text math, unambiguous ordering. Where the entry carries test_cases, this must be evaluable by tools/run_tests.py.

source_render.description: URL of the published image, when the regulation publishes the formula as a raster rather than as text. Its presence is the claim that the image was read.

variables.description: Every symbol appearing in the expression must be declared.

resolves_to.description: For graph-valued or cross-referenced terms: the entry id or figure that supplies the value.

operator.description: "==" only. "=" is not in the vocabulary — it reads as assignment and has already appeared in downstream copies of this schema.

value.description: A string when the bound is symbolic, e.g. "0.75 * P_k".

table.description: A lookup published by the regulation as a table. Rows are positional against columns so that a consumer can index without parsing prose.

applicability.description: Conditions under which this constraint does not apply. § 25.521(b) makes most of Subpart C a default path, not a hard requirement.

via.description: How to evaluate this case. Omitted: use this entry's own formula, or its breakpoints if it has them. "bound": check this entry's own bound predicate against inputs.value. Any other value: the id of the entry whose formula supplies the arithmetic — used where a bound constrains a quantity that another entry computes, so the check stays a real evaluation instead of a restated constant.

status.description: "worked" is earned by tools/run_tests.py, not asserted by an author. CI fails if a worked case does not reproduce.
